results.summary: This is a simple binary counter implemented in Wokwi that drives a 7-segment display. The eight outputs map directly to the seven segments and decimal point, and the design counts in binary at a 10 Hz clock. It requires no external hardware and is tested simply by turning it on. The documentation is very thin and the description is informal, so little can be said about its internal structure.

This design displays a user-selectable Latin character on a 7-segment display based on a 6-bit binary value entered on DIP switches. It drives the display one segment at a time, so a high clock rate is needed to see the full character. The character set covers a-z plus space, underscore, hyphen, period, exclamation mark and quote. Silicon tests report it working, and it is notable as a simple character generator with a documented mapping table.

This project adds two 4-bit numbers entered on the eight inputs and shows the 5-bit sum on the outputs, which are wired to a 7-segment display. It was created for Supercon 2023 as a tapeout test of basic logic gates that add things. The documentation does not explain how to test it beyond a placeholder, and the internal implementation is not described. It appears to be a simple educational adder demonstration rather than a complex design.

This design generates a VGA signal that displays a white pixel on a blue background, reusing VGA Flappy Bird code from Cutout1. It correctly times the sync and color signals for VGA output on the eight pins, which match the Tiny VGA pinout. It requires an external VGA adaptor and a digital-to-analog converter to connect to a monitor. The project was submitted for Supercon 2023 and is notable for being a minimal VGA demonstration on a Tiny Tapeout tile.
